title: MediaStream in HTMLMediaElement: Does it have a first frame?
body:
https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#handling-first-frame-available

> If the element is not eligible for autoplay, then the user agent must abort these substeps\.
> 
> The user agent may run the following substeps:​
> 
>     Set the paused attribute to false\.
>     If the element's show poster flag is true, set it to false and run the time marches on steps\.
>     Queue a task to fire an event named play at the element\.
>     Notify about playing for the element\.

This is the text for when a media element that's eligible for autoplay will start playing, after reaching HAVE_ENOUGH_DATA.

When a media element is playing a MediaStream this becomes a paradox:
- On one hand autoplay should start when the first frame is displayed (for MediaStreams we go directly to HAVE_ENOUGH_DATA when there's data since there's no buffering)
- On the other hand there's no natural "first frame" since there's no buffering (if the first frame of a video track is displayed and we play() the media element, there will always be a jump to the current frame, which could look completely different)

To me this boils down to whether a MediaStream can be considered having a "first frame" or not. If it can that would solve this spec issue -- but if so, what should its "first frame" be? If it cannot, we need to change the spec.

The same issue re-phrased could be whether a HTMLVideoElement which is playing a MediaStream that has a video track but is paused should advance past HAVE_METADATA? Per mediacapture-main the preload attribute is always "none" so that suggests an answer of No -- but then autoplaying this video element does not work.

FWIW Firefox currently (Nightly is now 65) does not advance the readyState past HAVE_METADATA until we're playing. But if the autoplay attribute is set we start playing before reaching HAVE_ENOUGH_DATA in order to work around this paradox. I.e., "playing" can happen already in HAVE_NOTHING.
